purpose: Reference data mapping each curriculum system (present in schools.json) to its stream/subject structure at Grade 9-12 level, so the expo app can conditionally show/hide questions and course-interest options based on a visitor's declared curriculum + stream + subjects (e.g. a PCMB/Science student should not be shown Commerce-only questions).

Indian.label: Indian / CBSE (and equivalent Indian boards)
Indian.note: Students pick ONE stream after Grade 10, then subjects within it. Streams are mutually exclusive in practice (a Science student does not also take Commerce papers), so the app should treat stream as the primary filter and subjects as a refinement within it.

IB.label: IB Diploma Programme (IBDP)
IB.note: Students pick ONE subject from each of the 6 groups (3 at Higher Level, 3 at Standard Level) plus the DP core (TOK, Extended Essay, CAS). No hard exclusions between groups, but the group-4/group-5 choices signal STEM leaning and group-3/group-6 choices signal humanities/arts leaning.

British.label: UK / British (IGCSE + A-Level)
British.note: Students typically pick 3 (sometimes 4) A-Level subjects with no formal 'stream' label, but combinations cluster around career direction. Use the combination clusters below to infer course-interest leaning; don't hard-exclude anything since mixed combinations (e.g. Maths + Biology + Art) are common.

subjects: Further Mathematics or Chemistry or Computer Science

American.label: American (US high school diploma, incl. AP)
American.structure: subject-area electives (AP is the advanced signal)
American.note: US diploma has broad required core (English, Maths, Science, Social Studies, PE) plus electives; AP course choice is the best signal of academic direction. No hard exclusions.

UAE MoE.label: UAE Ministry of Education (public / national curriculum)
UAE MoE.note: As of the current MoE reform, Grades 9-12 use four streams rather than the old 'scientific vs literary' split. All students share a compulsory core; streams mainly change the depth of Maths/Science and add electives.

streams.label: General Stream
streams.note: Default path from Grade 1; can continue after Grade 9.

streams.label: Advanced Stream
streams.note: Available after Grade 9 for high performers; deeper Maths & Science instruction.

streams.label: Professional / Vocational Stream
streams.note: Available after Grade 8; practical, applied curriculum.

streams.label: Elite Stream (Advanced Science Program)
streams.note: For academically outstanding students from Grade 6; heavy Maths/Science emphasis.

SABIS.label: SABIS Educational System (network curriculum, exam-aligned)
SABIS.note: SABIS is its own K-12 system used across many private schools regardless of nationality; it prepares students toward whichever external exams the school offers (IGCSE/A-Level and/or SAT/AP), so treat a SABIS visitor like the British or American model depending on which external track their specific school follows - ask if unsure.

Other.label: Other national curricula present in small numbers (French, German, Iranian, Pakistani, Philippine, Canadian, Bangladeshi, Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Russian, Australian)
Other.structure: not individually researched - low volume in this dataset
Other.note: Each of these has fewer than 10 schools across the three emirates. Rather than building a full subject model for each, the app should fall back to a generic 'What subjects are you currently studying / most interested in?' free-choice question (multi-select across a broad subject list) for visitors from these curricula, and let staff follow up in person. Revisit only if on-the-day volume from one of these curricula turns out to be significant.

app_integration_notes: Registration flow: after school-name autocomplete selects a school, auto-fill curriculum from schools.json (curriculum_tags[0]); if a school has 2 tags (e.g. dual American/IB schools), ask the visitor to confirm which track they're on.

Once curriculum is known, show the matching stream/subject picker above instead of a generic subject list - this directly implements the stakeholder's 'PCMB excludes Commerce' filtering request for Indian/CBSE, and gives an equivalent filter for British/American/IB/UAE MoE.
Use each stream/cluster's typical_course_interest array to pre-suggest (not force) course-interest options later in the flow, saving the visitor clicks.
For curricula in the 'Other' bucket, skip stream filtering entirely and use the generic subject multi-select.
